video.title: How Anyone Can Make $10K+/Month From the Government

summary: Natalie describes bidding as a prime contractor on government contracts, then hiring subcontractors to do the work and keeping the difference between their quote and her bid. She discusses contracts for hazardous waste disposal, catering, landscaping and relocation assistance, as well as using AI and public procurement data to evaluate bids. Her claimed earnings and low maintenance time depend on finding reliable subcontractors and doing substantial research and proposal work up front. Chris Koerner adds a post-interview clarification about subcontracting limits, certification programs and the legal risk of pass-through schemes.

speakers.name: Natalie
speakers.description: Government contractor and subcontracting prime; her full name is not stated.

ideas.name: Government contract prime and subcontractor broker
ideas.one_liner: Find public-sector contract opportunities, bid as the prime, hire a qualified subcontractor to perform the work and retain the difference.
ideas.business_model: Contract revenue with a markup over subcontractor cost; the prime invoices the government and pays the subcontractor.
ideas.customer: Federal, state, city and local government agencies, schools and universities procuring goods or services.
ideas.problem: Public bodies need vendors to complete work, while many small businesses know their trade but not the procurement and proposal process.
ideas.offer: Identify a suitable solicitation, prepare and submit a compliant bid, arrange subcontracted delivery and manage invoicing and contract coordination.

pricing.model: Bid a contract price based on the scope and subcontractor quote; retain the margin after paying delivery costs.
pricing.notes: No standard fee or markup is stated. Contract prices depend on the solicitation and past pricing.

acquisition_channels.details: Search SAM.gov and other public procurement systems for solicitations; she also says opportunities exist with local, state, city, school and university procurement systems.

quote.text: So the average person, how do they become a small business, well, just by having an LLC?
quote.speaker: Natalie

acquisition_channels.details: Find subcontractors who can perform the work, request a quote and confirm they are willing to work before submitting the bid.

quote.text: I always get a quote first, right? And get somebody that's willing to work before submit, right?
quote.speaker: Natalie

ideas.delivery: Natalie submits the proposal and acts as the prime contractor. Subcontractors perform most of the contracted service; she coordinates with them and invoices the government. The prime remains responsible for contract performance.
unit_economics_claims: See metric claims about contract prices, subcontractor costs, profit, payment timing, bid outcomes and maintenance hours.
ideas.startup_cost: Natalie says SAM.gov registration is free and that a business, internet and a phone are needed. She gives state LLC filing fees of $1-$300.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated. Natalie says her first contract bid was the first one she won, but gives no elapsed time.

acquisition.how: Agents can monitor public tender listings, filter scopes and deadlines, and flag likely fits. A person should approve bids and review procurement requirements. UK outreach to prospective subcontractors must follow PECR and calling rules; tender portals are inbound.

onboarding.how: Forms, document collection and reminders can be automated, but a person must confirm eligibility, subcontractor capability and the contract terms.

delivery.how: Subcontractors do the contracted work, but the work described includes physical services and the prime remains accountable for performance and problems.

billing.how: Invoice preparation and payment reminders can be automated; Natalie says she submits an invoice to maintain contracts.

support.how: Agents can triage routine questions, but service problems, subcontractor failures and government contract changes need human coordination.

uk_applicability.notes: The prime-and-subcontractor model can work in the UK, but this account relies on US procurement systems, eligibility rules and contract practices. A UK operator would need to use UK tender portals and follow UK procurement, tax and subcontracting requirements.

risks: The host's post-interview clarification says some contracts require the prime to perform at least 50% of the work and describes a 50% subcontract payment cap with an exception for qualifying small-business subcontractors.
The host warns that doing no strategy, consulting or coordination can make an arrangement an illegal pass-through scheme.
The prime is responsible to the government if a subcontractor fails, misses work or needs replacing.
A bid can be rejected for missing submission requirements or incorrect formatting even if the bidder can perform the work.
The host says government solicitations can specify local presence, past performance, subcontracting conditions or other evaluation criteria.
Payments may arrive on net 30 or net 45 terms, so contract cash flow and subcontractor payment terms need to be managed.
In the UK, unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals and sole traders is restricted under PECR; cold calls must be screened against TPS or CTPS as applicable.

ideas.name: Hazardous waste and formalin disposal contracts
ideas.one_liner: Win a government hazardous-waste pickup contract and subcontract the disposal work to a specialist provider.
ideas.business_model: Per-pickup contract revenue with a markup over the disposal company's quote.
ideas.customer: Government agencies needing periodic hazardous-waste pickup and disposal.
ideas.problem: Agencies need a qualified provider to collect and dispose of specified hazardous waste.
ideas.offer: Arrange pickup and disposal through a subcontracted hazardous-waste company.

pricing.model: Per pickup; the government price is set above the subcontractor quote.
pricing.notes: Natalie says the solicitation estimated 14 to 16 pickups a year and described a five-year contract.

acquisition_channels.details: She found the opportunity as a government contract listing.
She searched for hazardous-waste companies and contacted providers to get a quote before submitting.

quote.text: I was contacting different hazardous waste companies, because I knew at least that's what it revolved around.
quote.speaker: Natalie

ideas.delivery: A subcontracted hazardous-waste company performs the pickups and disposal. Natalie submits the bid and pays the subcontractor after receiving government payment.
unit_economics_claims: The stated subcontractor and government prices imply a $800 difference per pickup before other costs.
Natalie estimates 14 to 16 pickups a year and describes the arrangement as a five-year contract.

acquisition.how: Agents can monitor public tender listings and identify hazardous-waste scopes. A person should verify licensing, geography, bid terms and subcontractor availability.

onboarding.how: Document requests and bid intake can be automated, but a person should verify the subcontractor's qualifications and scope.

delivery.how: The subcontractor must physically collect and dispose of hazardous waste, so delivery depends on licensed people and equipment.

billing.how: Invoices and payment tracking can be automated after each pickup is documented.

support.how: Agents can route routine status requests, but pickup failures and hazardous-waste compliance issues need human attention.

uk_applicability.notes: The contracting pattern can transfer, but UK hazardous-waste handling, carrier registration and disposal requirements would need to be met.

risks: Hazardous-waste work requires an appropriately qualified subcontractor and compliance with relevant handling and disposal rules.
If the provider misses a pickup or cannot perform the contract, the prime remains accountable.

quotes.text: I submitted the proposal with their quote. I put my quote on top. They submitted a quote for like 700 and I submitted a quote for 1500 and I won.
quotes.speaker: Natalie

ideas.name: Government and military catering contracts
ideas.one_liner: Bid to provide meals to a government facility and hire a local caterer to prepare and deliver them.
ideas.business_model: Per-meal contract pricing with a markup over the catering subcontractor's per-meal rate.
ideas.customer: A government facility or camp needing meals for soldiers.
ideas.problem: The facility needs breakfast, lunch and dinner delivered daily for a defined period.
ideas.offer: Arrange and manage meal delivery through a local catering business.

pricing.notes: The contract covered breakfast, lunch and dinner for two weeks. The transcript does not clearly state the number of diners.

acquisition_channels.details: Natalie found and bid on the government catering contract.
She contacted a catering company in Idaho; it had previously worked with the facility.

quote.text: I went and contacted a catering company over in Idaho. Turns out they had already worked with that camp that facility already previously.
quote.speaker: Natalie

ideas.delivery: The catering subcontractor prepared and delivered meals, removed waste and returned daily for two weeks. Natalie managed the contract as prime.
unit_economics_claims: The subcontractor charged $41,000 and Natalie charged the government $52,000, which she says yielded $11,000 profit over two weeks.

acquisition.how: Tender monitoring can be automated; a person must confirm the caterer can meet the location, menu, volume and schedule.

onboarding.how: Forms and document collection can be automated, but food-service capability and contract requirements need review.

delivery.how: Preparing and delivering meals and removing waste are physical tasks performed by the caterer.

billing.how: Invoice creation and tracking can be automated after delivery records are received.

support.how: Meal, timing or food-safety problems need prompt human coordination with the caterer and customer.

uk_applicability.notes: Catering contracts are common in the UK, but local food-safety, allergen and procurement requirements would apply.

risks: The caterer must be able to deliver reliably each day and meet the facility's requirements.
Meal volume, food safety and delivery logistics affect costs; the transcript does not state all contract expenses.

quotes.text: It was for two weeks. It was for to feed soldiers, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for two weeks.
quotes.speaker: Natalie

ideas.name: Government landscaping and snow-management contracts
ideas.one_liner: Win a multi-year landscaping contract and use a local crew to provide the grounds work.
ideas.business_model: Multi-year service contract with subcontracted work and a margin between the subcontractor cost and government award.
ideas.customer: Government agencies or facilities needing landscaping and related site services.
ideas.problem: Facilities need regular grounds maintenance; winter work may also require site visits or snow-season planning.
ideas.offer: Arrange landscaping service through a subcontractor and manage the government contract.

pricing.model: Multi-year contract award; exact payment schedule and scope vary by contract.
pricing.notes: Natalie also recounts that the scope was initially priced at $800,000 with a $500,000 subcontractor quote before a modification; the transcript's final modified amount is stated unclearly in that passage.

acquisition_channels.details: Find and bid on government landscaping solicitations.
Engage a local landscaping subcontractor able to provide the work; Natalie describes a Colorado crew of six.

ideas.delivery: A landscaping crew performs the site work. Natalie says she visited the Colorado site before snow season, although she was told a FaceTime walkthrough was also an option.
unit_economics_claims: Natalie says a subcontractor quoted $700,000 against a $962,000 five-year contract.
She says she later found a previous contract for the same work at $1.6 million.

acquisition.how: Agents can monitor tender portals and extract scope, location and bid dates; people must assess the site and verify subcontractor capacity.

onboarding.how: Document collection and compliance reminders can be automated, with human review of the subcontractor and site requirements.

delivery.how: Landscaping and snow-related site work are physical tasks requiring a local crew.

billing.how: Scheduled invoices and payment tracking can be automated against completed work records.

support.how: Agents can handle routine status updates, but site issues, scope disputes and weather-related changes require human coordination.

uk_applicability.notes: Public-sector landscaping is applicable in the UK, though contract specifications, seasonal conditions and procurement requirements vary.

risks: The physical work depends on a reliable crew and local site knowledge.
A scope omission can create cost disputes; Natalie says she sought a contract modification when the site work differed from the written scope.
Past award prices are a guide, not a guarantee of current price or award.

ideas.name: Relocation assistance for a government-affected resident
ideas.one_liner: Help a resident whose home is being acquired by the government find and move into an apartment under a paid contract.
ideas.business_model: Fixed-price service contract with progress payments.
ideas.customer: A government agency arranging relocation support for a resident whose home is being taken for a public project.
ideas.problem: The resident needed help finding an apartment, applying and getting approved after the government acquired her home.
ideas.offer: Help search for housing, visit properties, assist with applications and coordinate the move.

pricing.model: Fixed contract price with progress payments.
pricing.notes: Natalie says travel expenses needed to be included in her price.

acquisition_channels.details: Natalie found a government relocation contract bid.

ideas.delivery: Natalie performed the work herself: she travelled to Virginia, met the resident, viewed properties with her, helped her apply and get approved, and arranged progress payments.
unit_economics_claims: Natalie says she priced the contract at $14,000 and received progress payments of $5,000, $5,000 and $4,000.
The host estimated that she may have earned over $1,000 per hour; the transcript gives no hours or expense total to verify that estimate.

onboarding.how: Forms and appointment reminders can be automated, but the resident's needs and applications require personal support.

delivery.how: Natalie met the resident and visited properties in person; the service involves human judgment and physical travel.

billing.how: Progress invoices can be scheduled and tracked once milestones are documented.

support.how: Housing applications and a person's relocation needs require direct human help.

uk_applicability.notes: Relocation support can be contracted in the UK, but the legal basis, housing process and public-sector requirements would differ.

risks: Travel and accommodation costs need to be included in the bid.
The service depends on trust and personal support for a resident facing displacement.

tactics.name: Choose a bid you can understand and deliver
steps: Read the solicitation and its attachments before committing to a bid.

Confirm that a subcontractor can do the work and provide the required information before submitting.

quote.text: My very first step on what I do is look for something that I understand what they're looking for.

tactics.name: Get a subcontractor quote before bidding
steps: Search for providers in the contract's location and service category.
Ask for a quote and confirm willingness to work before submitting the proposal.
Do not rely on a supplier who is slow to respond or reluctant to take the work.
Check reviews, website, prior work and apparent credibility; seek a contingency provider after winning.

quote.text: I always get a quote first, right? And get somebody that's willing to work before submit, right?

tactics.name: Use a broad business name

tactics.name: Check past award pricing before setting a bid
steps: Search USAspending.gov for prior contracts, contractors, agency spend and relevant industry codes.
Compare the prior contract and scope with the current solicitation.
Account for inflation and the current scope when setting a price; do not assume the government will accept a high markup.

Use AI to help draft the proposal, then check all instructions and facts yourself.

tactics.name: Follow the evaluation criteria exactly
steps: Read each solicitation's evaluation criteria.
Check whether it requires local presence, past performance, a particular price approach or limits on subcontracting.
Skip opportunities whose mandatory conditions cannot be met.

quote.text: On every single contract, they give you an evaluation criteria. On every single contract, they tell you this is what they're looking for.

tactics.name: Build a niche after learning the process
steps: Use early bids to learn the submission process and test what is understandable and deliverable.

tactics.name: Keep reliable subcontractors and a backup
steps: Look for responsiveness, strong communication, credibility and a real need for the work.
Review the provider's reviews, website and previous work.
Find a contingency subcontractor after a contract is awarded.
Raise scope or performance problems with the government early and propose a solution.
